title: Bit manipulation
learn: binary representation, &, |, ^, ~, <<, >>, XOR tricks (a^a=0), n & (n-1), masks
hook: Single Number, Number of 1 Bits, Counting Bits and Missing Number have one-line bitwise answers that interviewers love. They're quick wins, and they show you understand how numbers are stored.

explain.prompt: Explain how XOR finds the single number in an array where every other number appears twice, and what n & (n − 1) does.
keyPoints: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, and XOR is order-independent
XOR all numbers: every pair cancels, leaving the single one; O(n) time, O(1) space
n & (n − 1) clears the lowest set bit, so looping it counts set bits in O(number of 1-bits)
n > 0 and n & (n − 1) == 0 means n is a power of two
Python ints are unbounded: mask with 0xFFFFFFFF to imitate 32-bit behaviour
